messages:
maria_support: FYI ACME reported a big p95 spike (~7s) + intermittent 429s on their dedicated pool (dp-34, eu-west-2) last night around 23:10 UTC. They also flagged a billing overage. They say MIG config is 1g.5gb.
kevin_sre: Can you paste the pool id, node ids and any recent deploys? Also did autoscale trigger?
maria_support: Pool dp-34, nodes: host-eu2-12 / host-eu2-15. No deploys in that window. Autoscale log shows no scale-up because available capacity reported 0/2 spare slots. Pasting snippets: 
```
[2026-02-12T23:09:51Z] auth-proxy: 502 upstream error -> fallback to 429 after 30s
[2026-02-12T23:10:05Z] inference: p95 7200ms, p50 120ms
[2026-02-12T23:10:06Z] billing: usage spikes +12% vs baseline
```
jess_oncall: Do we have SM/SM util and NVlink metrics for those hosts? Noise often shows up as one slice saturating SMs.
ryan_prodeng: I suspect noisy-slice crosstalk on MIG packing. If a heavy tenant got fractional-packed with ACME on the same host it can push SM% and L3 thrash. Ask SRE to grab `nvidia-smi dmon` / `telegraf` timeseries around 23:05-23:15.
infra_bot: alert: host-eu2-15 gpu_sm_util > 95% for 00:03 (rule: gpu_sm_high). incident_id=INC-20260212-883
kevin_sre: Running quick check now — pulling `redwoodctl inspect pool dp-34 --since 2026-02-12T23:00Z`. Also check `redwoodctl events --pool dp-34`.
maria_support: Paste of `redwoodctl inspect` (trimmed):
```
pool: dp-34
nodes:
 - host-eu2-12 mig=1g.5gb slices: 4
 - host-eu2-15 mig=1g.5gb slices: 4
observed: burst auth 5xx -> 429 fallback
autoscale: desired=6 actual=6 max=6 (hit cap)
```
ryan_prodeng: Autoscaler hit the pool cap — so no spare nodes to move a noisy tenant. That matches the customer seeing 429s (no place to schedule). We should repro locally by co-locating a noisy generator on a slice.
kevin_sre: I ran a quick repro on host-eu2-15 in staging: with a synthetic chat load (4 concurrent streams, avg token length 600) on a co-located tenant we see p95 jump from 150ms -> 3.2s and per-slice SM util 92-98%.
maria_support: ACME provided a short sample curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"<~600 tokens>","max_tokens":512}'
```
jess_oncall: Short-term mitigation: move ACME to an isolated reserved slot or evict the noisy tenant. Long-term: increase pool cap or relax fractional packing for this pool.
billing_ops: About the billing overage — if we moved them temporarily to reserved capacity we should credit their unexpected egress/compute spike during triage window. I'll open a billing ticket.
ryan_prodeng: Quick config note: fractional packing policy for dp-34 is `pack_aggressive=true` — that's the risky bit. Recommend `pack_threshold=0.6` for this pool for safer isolation.
kevin_sre: For next steps I did: 1) quarantined suspected noisy tenant (tenant-x123) from host-eu2-15 2) repro test after quarantine showed ACME p95 back to ~180ms 3) created evict job + migration job for tenant-x123 -> host-eu2-22 (isolated). Logs: 
```
[2026-02-12T23:22:10Z] evict tenant-x123 -> drain host-eu2-15
[2026-02-12T23:27:03Z] acme p95 180ms
```
maria_support: ACME confirms latency improved and 429s stopped. They asked about the unexpected bill spike — billing_ops will follow.
billing_ops: Opened BILL-4527 to adjust charges for ACME for 2026-02-12 23:00-23:40 UTC while we triaged.
kevin_sre: Posting follow-up actions: - change dp-34 pack policy to safer defaults - add scale-up buffer to autoscaler when pool concurrency > 80% - incident postmortem and runbook update for noisy-slice detection (include `nvidia-smi dmon` & `sm_util` thresholds).
maria_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and mark the thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:
jess_oncall: I'll own the postmortem and slot policy change.
ryan_prodeng: Also let's add an automated detector that correlates auth-5xx spikes + sm_util surge -> auto-evict candidate.
maria_support: Closing loop: moved ACME to reserved slot dp-34-rsv, billing adjusted, monitoring shows stable p95. Will file postmortem link when ready.
